title: Privacy Statement
content:
Last updated: 03/08/2026

Stockgrove Brickhill Systems Ltd  ("we", "us" or "our") respects your privacy and is committed to protecting personal information.

This Privacy Statement explains how we collect, use and protect personal information when you visit our website, contact us about our services, or engage us to provide Python, Django, software development or technical consultancy services.

1. Who we are

Stockgrove Brickhill Systems Ltd is a company registered in England and Wales under company number 06438539.

Registered office:

The Barn

Pear Tree Lane

Whitchurch

Shropshire  SY13 1NG

Email: /contact

For the purposes of UK data protection legislation, we are the data controller for personal information that we collect and use in connection with our business, except where we process information on behalf of a client as a data processor.

2. Information we collect

Depending on how you interact with us, we may collect:

Information you provide to us

This may include:

  • your name;

  • business name and job title;

  • email address;

  • telephone number;

  • business address;

  • information contained in enquiries or correspondence;

  • project requirements and specifications;

  • information required to provide quotations and invoices; and

  • other information you voluntarily provide to us.

Information collected when you use our website

Our website may automatically collect limited technical information, such as:

  • IP address;

  • browser type and version;

  • operating system;

  • referring website;

  • pages visited;

  • date and time of visits; and

  • technical information about how you interact with our website.

The precise information collected depends on the hosting, analytics and other services used by our website.

3. How we use your information

We may use personal information to:

  • respond to enquiries;

  • discuss and quote for potential projects;

  • provide software development and consultancy services;

  • communicate with clients;

  • manage projects and deliverables;

  • administer contracts;

  • issue and manage invoices and payments;

  • maintain business records;

  • provide technical support;

  • maintain and improve our website and services;

  • protect the security of our systems;

  • comply with legal and regulatory obligations; and

  • establish, exercise or defend legal claims.

We will only use personal information where we have a lawful basis for doing so.

4. Lawful bases for processing

Depending on the circumstances, we may rely on one or more of the following lawful bases under UK data protection legislation:

Contract

We may process information where it is necessary to enter into or perform a contract with you.

For example, we may need your contact details and business information to provide a quotation, agree a project and deliver the services.

Legitimate interests

We may process information where it is necessary for our legitimate business interests and those interests are not overridden by your rights.

This may include managing business relationships, responding to enquiries, improving our services, maintaining security and protecting our business.

Legal obligation

We may process information where necessary to comply with legal obligations, including accounting, tax and financial record-keeping requirements.

Consent

Where required, we may ask for your consent before processing personal information for a particular purpose. Where processing is based on consent, you may withdraw that consent at any time.

5. Enquiries and contact forms

If you contact us through our website, by email or by another means, we will use the information you provide to respond to your enquiry and, where appropriate, discuss or provide our services.

We may retain correspondence and enquiry information for a reasonable period in order to maintain appropriate business records and follow up potential engagements.

6. Client information

If you engage us to provide services, we may process information about you and other individuals involved in the project.

This may include names, contact details, job titles, business information, correspondence, project requirements and information necessary to administer the contract.

We will use this information only for legitimate business purposes connected with the engagement.

7. Information processed on behalf of clients

During software development or consultancy work, we may sometimes access information belonging to a client or hosted within a client's systems.

Where we process personal data solely on behalf of a client and in accordance with the client's instructions, the client will generally be the data controller and we will act as a data processor.

In those circumstances, our processing will be governed by the applicable contractual and data-processing arrangements with the client.

8. Sharing personal information

We do not sell personal information.

We may share information where reasonably necessary with:

  • professional advisers such as accountants, solicitors or insurers;

  • hosting and infrastructure providers;

  • software and IT service providers;

  • payment providers;

  • email and communication service providers;

  • subcontractors assisting us with a project; or

  • government, regulatory or law-enforcement authorities where required or permitted by law.

Where we use service providers to process personal information on our behalf, we will take reasonable steps to ensure that appropriate contractual and security arrangements are in place.

9. International transfers

Some service providers we use may process information outside the United Kingdom.

Where personal information is transferred internationally, we will take appropriate steps to ensure that the transfer is made in accordance with applicable data protection legislation and that appropriate safeguards are in place where required.

10. How long we keep information

We retain personal information only for as long as reasonably necessary for the purposes for which it was collected.

The appropriate retention period depends on the type of information and why we need it.

For example, financial and accounting records may need to be retained for longer periods to comply with legal and tax requirements.

We may also retain information for as long as necessary to establish, exercise or defend legal claims.

When information is no longer required, we will securely delete it or otherwise dispose of it appropriately.

11. Website analytics and cookies

Our website may use cookies or similar technologies.

Some cookies are necessary for the website to operate correctly. Other cookies may be used for purposes such as analytics, measuring website usage or improving the website.

Where required, we will ask for your consent before placing non-essential cookies on your device.

You can manage cookies through your browser and, where provided, our website's cookie controls.

For further information, please see our Cookie Policy.

12. Security

We take reasonable technical and organisational measures to protect personal information against unauthorised access, loss, misuse, alteration or disclosure.

However, no internet transmission or electronic storage system can be guaranteed to be completely secure.

Where we are given access to client systems as part of a project, we will take reasonable steps to protect credentials and information provided to us.

13. Your rights

Subject to applicable legal conditions and exemptions, you may have rights under UK data protection law to:

  • request access to personal information we hold about you;

  • request correction of inaccurate or incomplete information;

  • request deletion of personal information;

  • request restriction of processing;

  • object to certain processing;

  • request transfer of certain information to another organisation; and

  • withdraw consent where processing is based on consent.

You may also have the right to object to direct marketing.

To exercise a right, please contact us using the details below.

We may need to verify your identity before responding to a request.

14. Complaints

If you have concerns about how we have handled your personal information, please contact us first so that we have an opportunity to investigate and resolve the matter.

You also have the right to complain to the UK's data protection regulator:

Information Commissioner's Office (ICO)

You can find information about making a complaint on the ICO's website.

Information Commissioner's Office

15. Changes to this Privacy Statement

We may update this Privacy Statement from time to time to reflect changes to our business, website, services, technology or legal requirements.

The latest version will be published on this page with the date of the most recent update shown at the top.

16. Contact us

If you have questions about this Privacy Statement, want to exercise your data protection rights, or have a concern about how we process personal information, please contact us:
